message.content: {"12731_8353800651455": {"answer": "B", "reason": "Scimitar syndrome is characterized by right lung hypoplasia (often with upper lobe aplasia) causing volume loss and dextroposition of the heart, alongside an anomalous pulmonary vein."}, "12731_8353800681488": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The chest X-ray demonstrates a small, opaque right hemithorax with the heart shifted to the right (dextroposition), consistent with right upper lobe aplasia and Scimitar syndrome."}, "12731_8353800681938": {"answer": "B", "reason": "In this variant of Scimitar syndrome, the mediastinal shift to the right (dextroposition) is primarily caused by volume loss due to the aplasia or severe hypoplasia of the right upper lobe."}, "12731_8353800704154": {"answer": "C", "reason": "The scimitar vein typically courses along the right heart border draining into the IVC, and in cases with right lung hypoplasia/aplasia, the mediastinum deviates to the right; systemic arterial supply often arises inferiorly from the aorta."}}
